narrative.summary: Moldova has no AI law or adopted AI strategy yet. Its AI governance rests on the economic development and digitalisation ministry's (MDED) declarative 2024 White Paper on Artificial Intelligence and Data Governance. In 2026 the ministry put the concept of a National Programme on AI and Data Governance 2026-2030 to public consultation and began work on an AI law aligned with the EU AI Act. The 2024 personal data protection law, in force since August 2026, regulates automated decision-making and profiling, and a 2024 presidential decree approved signing the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI. Moldova is a party to the Council of Europe's data protection convention (Convention 108).
lead_institutions: Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization (MDED)

narrative.review_notes: On 18 October 2026 the Official Gazette, government, ministry, consultation portal, data protection authority and National Bank websites were checked again; the 2024 data protection law and the 2024 decree on the AI convention were read in the Official Gazette. Not yet verified from the official text: the AI content of the 2023 Digital Transformation Strategy and the electoral code amendments.

instruments.english_title: White Paper on Artificial Intelligence and Data Governance
instruments.current_status: Published by MDED on 2 October 2024 (ministry page dated 02/10/2024, with Romanian and English versions linked from the page; the PDF states 'Chișinău, 2024', manuscript finalised August 2024, first edition). An earlier draft was put to repeated public consultation on particip.gov.md from 21.02.2024 to 31.03.2024. The document describes itself as a declarative policy document reflecting the Government's position, not a policy document proper. The 2026 concept of the National Programme on AI and Data Governance 2026-2030 describes it as the first (declarative) policy framework in the field and says the Programme will implement it.
instruments.summary: Declarative policy paper of the Government of Moldova, drafted by the MDED Sub-Council for AI and Data Governance, setting the national vision for AI and data governance aligned with EU standards. It sets four general objectives (education and skills, resilient infrastructure and reusable datasets, trustworthy AI adoption, a governance and regulatory framework) and nine key requirements for AI systems (interoperability, human agency, transparency and explainability, safety and security, adaptability, accountability, accessibility, sustainability, data privacy). It recommends a comprehensive AI and data governance regulatory framework, an ethics framework and a national AI regulatory sandbox, to guide central public administration in standardising and regulating AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Moldova's first AI policy framework; reference document for the planned National Programme on AI and Data Governance 2026-2030 and an AI law.

instruments.current_status: Concept published on particip.gov.md (ID 16590) at the drafting-initiation stage, consultation window 28.04.2026-12.05.2026 (1 comment submitted). The concept says the Programme will be approved by Government decision and drafted in Q2 2026; no draft Programme or adopted decision was found on official sites as of 2026-10-13.
instruments.summary: Concept note for a five-year national AI and data governance programme, to be approved by Government decision, which would detail the AI component of the Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030 and operationalise the 2024 White Paper. It proposes five objectives: a national AI regulatory framework aligned with the EU AI Act, AI education and up/reskilling, digital infrastructure (HPC, interoperable data), AI R&D and adoption in strategic sectors, and AI in public administration (e-government, anti-corruption). It identifies the lack of a national competent authority for AI and of a comprehensive AI law as key gaps.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First planned public-policy document dedicated to AI in Moldova; signals a future AI regulatory framework and competent authority.

instruments.english_title: Law No. 195 of 25 July 2024 on personal data protection
instruments.current_status: Adopted 25 July 2024 and published in the Official Gazette (Monitorul Oficial) No. 367-369 of 23 August 2024, art. 574, together with promulgation decree No. 1592-IX of 21 August 2024. Article 89(1) provides that the law enters into force 24 months after its publication; the National Center for Personal Data Protection states that it entered into force on 23 August 2026.
instruments.summary: General personal data protection law modelled on the EU GDPR. Article 22 gives people the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them, with limited exceptions; controllers must inform people about such automated decision-making and the logic involved. It also requires data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing and prior consultation of the National Center for Personal Data Protection.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main binding rules in Moldova that apply to automated decision-making and profiling, including by AI systems that process personal data.

coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): This review was carried out on 13 October 2026, but the official legal database (legis.md), the Official Gazette's and Parliament's websites could not be accessed, so the 2024 data protection law and the Convention 108 ratification act could not be read. Moldova is marked for a later retry. The planned AI law, the 2024 data protection law and the AI sub-council's founding order are tracked as leads.

Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-13, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. legis.md 403 (curl and WebFetch); monitorul.gov.md 502; parlament.md 403; cec.md not searched; ANRCETI, Audiovisual Council, Competition Council not searched (web search budget exhausted). White Paper i-ccf09429a98d retitled, nonbinding_guidance (self-described declarative), PDF on Google Drive linked from MDED page; o-538745d916d8 and s-7bbf20c7d2c3 kept with corrected content. Law 195/2024 (in force 23-08-2026 per CNPDCP) text and MO date unreadable (lead). Convention 108: Parliament Decision 483-XIV of 2 July 1999 per CNPDCP page only (act on legis.md not read) - not attached; added to pending_c108. Units covered: Law: legis.md, monitorul.gov.md and parlament.md unreachable (HTTP 403/502 to curl; legis.md 403 to WebFetch). Via other official hosts: no adopted AI law or AI-specific provisions found; AI law drafting initiated May 2026 (lead); data protection Law 195/2024 (lead, text unread); no deepfake/AI offence found in adopted law; Electoral Code AI amendments only at CEC drafting stage (lead).; Government: MDED (White Paper 2024 recorded; SCIA pages; site search), particip.gov.md (White Paper consultation, AI programme concept recorded, AI law notice lead), gov.md (Digital Transformation Strategy implementation programme draft: AI only in passing). No public-sector/GenAI guidelines found (e-Governance Agency, State Chancellery searched).; Ministries: Education and Research (mec.gov.md site search: nothing; AI-in-education act in preparation, lead); Labour, Interior only via MDED AI safety campaign press release (awareness campaign, no instrument); Health, Justice, Defence, Finance: searched, nothing found.; Regulators: CNPDCP (datepersonale.md: no AI-specific guidance; general Law 195/2024 guidance only), National Bank (bnm.md: AI rules announced, none published - lead), Cyber Security Agency and e-Governance Agency: searched, nothing found; CEC (lead). ANRCETI, Audiovisual Council, Competition Council: not reached (web search budget exhausted).. Not reached: legis.md (HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch); monitorul.gov.md (HTTP 502); parlament.md (HTTP 403); cec.md (not directly searched); ANRCETI, Audiovisual Council, Competition Council (not searched: web search budget exhausted).
